sentences.text: With passage of time and during the pendency of these petitions, the disputes have been resolved and consent terms have been executed between the parties in a pending proceeding before the Family Court at Bandra, Mumbai.
A proceeding for divorce is pending before the said Court in which the consent terms have been filed.
The parties have agreed to convert the said proceeding into proceeding for divorce by mutual consent.

4. Respondent No. 2 has sworn affidavits in both these petitions annexing copies of the consent terms stating that she has no objection for the prayers being granted, in the light of the dispute between the parties being resolved.
The affidavits also give details of all the other pending proceedings between the parties.

5. The consent terms show that upon the present proceedings being disposed of as also other proceedings culminating into consent orders, on 7th January 2026, the petition for divorce will be taken up before the Family Court at Bandra, Mumbai, when the petitioners shall pay a sum of Rs.15,00,000/- to respondent No. 2 for grant of such decree of divorce by mutual consent.

6. In other words, the consent affidavits in these petitions have been tendered by respondent No. 2 on a clear understanding that the aforesaid amount of Rs.15,00,000/- shall be paid to her in the proceedings before the Family Court at Bandra, Mumbai, on 7 th January 2026.
Rushikesh 901 WP.517.2022.doc 7.
The affidavits of respondent No. 2 in these two petitions are taken on record.

A perusal of the same, as also the copies of the consent terms annexed thereto, clearly shows the obligations of the petitioners as also the respondent No. 2.
8.
The petitioners as well as respondent No. 2 shall abide by their respective obligations as per the consent terms.

9. Since the instant FIR and the consequential criminal proceedings arose essentially out of matrimonial discord between petitioner No. 1 in Writ Petition No. 517 of 2022 and respondent No. 2 (first informant), we are inclined to allow these petitions with the consent of respondent No. 2.
10.
It is brought to our notice that as regards the petitioners in Writ Petition No. 518 of 2022, upon completion of investigation they have not been chargesheeted.
Yet, by way of abundant caution, the parties are agreeing to quashing of the FIR in the context of the said petitioners also..

11. In the case of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab1 the Supreme Court while considering the question of quashing of FIRs concerning non-compoundable offences, in paragraph 61 observed as follows:
"61.

sentences.text:
The position that emerges from the above discussion can be summarised thus:
the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint Nisha Gupta And Anr vs State Of Maharashtra on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155795852/
2 in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
Inherent power is of wide plenitude with no statutory limitation but it has to be exercised in 1 (2012) 10 SCC 303 Rushikesh 901 WP.517.2022.doc accord with the guideline engrafted in such power viz. : (i) to secure the ends of justice, or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any court.

entities.text: Nisha Gupta And Anr vs State Of Maharashtra on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In what cases power to quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or FIR may be exercised where the offender and the victim have settled their dispute would depend on the facts and circumstances of each case and no category can be prescribed.
However, before exercise of such power, the High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime.

Heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc.
cannot be fittingly quashed even though the victim or victim's family and the offender have settled the dispute.
Such offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society.

Similarly, any compromise between the victim and the offender in relation to the offences under special statutes like the Prevention of Corruption Act or the offences committed by public servants while working in that capacity, etc.; cannot provide for any basis for quashing criminal proceedings involving such offences.

But the criminal cases having overwhelmingly and predominatingly civil flavour stand on a different footing for the purposes of quashing, particularly the offences arising from commercial, financial, mercantile, civil, partnership or such like transactions or the offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, etc. or the family disputes where the wrong is basically private or personal in nature and the parties have resolved their entire dispute.

In this category of cases, the High Court may quash the criminal proceedings if in its view, because of the compromise between the offender and the victim, the possibility of conviction is remote and bleak and continuation of the criminal case would put the accused to great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal case despite full and complete settlement and compromise with the victim.

In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of the criminal Rushikesh 901 WP.517.2022.doc proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that the criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in the affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding."

12. Applying the said position of law to the facts of the present case, we find that no fruitful purpose will be served by allowing the criminal proceedings to continue and it would meet the ends of justice to allow these petitions.
13.
In view of the above, the petitions are allowed.

Consequently, FIR No. 430 of 2021 dated 25 th July 2021, registered at Nirmal Nagar Police Station, Mumbai, along with chargesheet filed in pursuance thereof, and Criminal Case No. PW/1956/2022, pending before the Judicial Magistrate First Class, 32nd Court at Bandra, Mumbai, are quashed.
